Repairing it is a behavioural change under decision 7: it changes how many reports a rejected sequence draws, and that needs its own corpus measurement, which this change did not make -- it measured where predicates are read and written, not the cardinality of ordering reports. The repair belongs to whoever revisits KEYPAIRGENERATOR-ORDER-00 with a corpus in hand; what is owed here is that the asymmetry stops being invisible. REPAIRED (gh105 task 9.2, 2026-08-25). The `__RESET;` is in the block and the asymmetry is gone: 21 of 21 `@fail` handlers reset. Two things the repair does not claim, both measured on the day it landed. The evidence is the generated monitor's `reset()` clearing the flag and this row, which is why task 9.2 sits in the block that needs no researcher decision: no program changes what it is accused of. `kp = null;` still clears one staged field while `algorithm` stays set -- the asymmetry with KeyGeneratorSpec.mop:169-176 that this row also named -- and that half is untouched.

So the 103 SSLContextSpec/SSL events of the published corpus did obtain a TLS context at run time, and this row exists so a reader of a report knows that. Contrast the TLS row, which IS a platform-value: TLS is the name the platform documents and the one an app wanting the current protocol is told to ask for.
